stem: What is the maximum number of cuttlefish the facility can house under this guideline?
stimulus: A marine research facility raises juvenile cuttlefish in 6 separate tanks: 4 tanks each hold $0.25$ cubic meters of seawater, and 2 tanks each hold $0.4$ cubic meters. The guideline requires at least 18 liters of seawater per cuttlefish in its tank. ($1$ cubic meter $= 1{,}000$ liters)
explanation: Work out each tank on its own, because a cuttlefish uses only the water in its own tank. A $0.25$ m³ tank holds $250$ L, and $250 \text{ L} \div 18 \text{ L/cuttlefish} \approx 13.9$, so it can hold at most 13 cuttlefish. A $0.4$ m³ tank holds $400$ L, and $400 \div 18 \approx 22.2$, so it can hold at most 22. That gives a total of $4(13) + 2(22) = 52 + 44 = 96$ cuttlefish.

A.why: You correctly found 13 per small tank and multiplied by 4 to get 52, but you stopped there. You still need to add the 44 cuttlefish that fit in the two larger tanks.

C.why: You added up all the water first ($1{,}800$ L) and divided by 18 to get exactly 100. The tanks are separate, so the leftover fraction of a cuttlefish's water in each tank cannot be combined with leftovers from other tanks. Round down tank by tank before you add.

D.why: You rounded $13.9$ up to 14 and $22.2$ up to 23. The guideline says at least 18 L per cuttlefish, so a partial share is not enough. Round each tank down to a whole number of cuttlefish.

stem: How many more hours than the godwit does the plover take to fly the route?
stimulus: Two tagged shorebirds each fly the same 2,700-kilometer migration route nonstop. A godwit flies at a constant speed of 60 kilometers per hour. A plover flies at a constant speed of 750 meters per minute.
explanation: First convert the plover's speed: $750 \tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{min}} \times \tfrac{60 \text{ min}}{1 \text{ h}} \times \tfrac{1 \text{ km}}{1{,}000 \text{ m}} = 45$ km/h. Time is distance divided by speed. The godwit takes $2{,}700 \div 60 = 45$ hours, and the plover takes $2{,}700 \div 45 = 60$ hours. The difference is $60 - 45 = 15$ hours.

B.why: 60 hours is how long the plover takes. The question asks how many more hours the plover needs than the godwit, so you still have to subtract the godwit's 45 hours.

C.why: You subtracted the speeds first ($60 - 45 = 15$ km/h) and then divided $2{,}700$ by 15. Time is distance ÷ speed for each bird separately. A difference of speeds does not give a difference of times. Find each bird's time, then subtract.

D.why: 900 is the difference in minutes ($3{,}600 - 2{,}700$). You worked in the plover's units and never converted back. The question asks for hours, and $900 \text{ min} \div 60 = 15$ hours.
